paper.title: ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-world APIs

summary.one_sentence: ToolLLM scales tool learning from API-call selection to multi-step REST API trajectories over 16,464 real-world APIs.
summary.thesis: Open-source LLMs need tool-specific instruction data, API retrieval, executable multi-step trajectories, and a planner that can backtrack when tool calls fail.
summary.why_it_matters: ToolLLM treats an agent as a system over a real API marketplace: catalog ingestion, API metadata, retriever precision, execution traces, evaluator design, and search strategy are all part of the same tool-use stack.

prior_state: General instruction tuning gave open-source LLMs broad dialogue skills but weak tool-use ability.
Earlier datasets often used limited APIs, single-tool settings, or no real API execution responses.
Users cannot manually choose the correct API subset when the available tool pool contains thousands of real APIs.
Linear ReAct-style reasoning can get stuck after a wrong API call because it explores only one trajectory.
problem.key_gap: The paper asks how to build, train, retrieve, plan, and evaluate open-source LLM tool use over a large real-world REST API marketplace with both single-tool and multi-tool tasks.
assumptions: RapidAPI documentation and example responses can be crawled and normalized into useful API metadata.
ChatGPT can generate candidate tool-use instructions and solution paths with minimal human supervision.
A decision-tree search over tool-use trajectories can produce better annotations than one-path ReAct.
An LLM-based evaluator can approximate human judgment for pass/fail and pairwise solution quality.

concepts.name: ToolBench
concepts.definition: An instruction-tuning dataset for tool use built from RapidAPI APIs, synthetic instructions, and annotated multi-step solution paths.

concepts.name: Depth-first search decision tree
concepts.definition: A reasoning strategy that explores multiple tool-use trajectories and can abandon failed branches instead of committing to one ReAct-style path.

concepts.name: ToolEval
concepts.definition: A ChatGPT-backed evaluator with pass-rate and win-rate metrics for judging whether tool-use trajectories complete an instruction and which trajectory is better.

concepts.name: Neural API retriever
concepts.definition: A dense retriever trained from generated instruction/API pairs to select relevant APIs from the large ToolBench API pool.

method.core_idea: Collect and filter RapidAPI tools, generate single-tool and multi-tool instructions with ChatGPT, annotate executable solution paths with DFSDT, finetune LLaMA-2 7B into ToolLLaMA, retrieve candidate APIs with a neural retriever, and evaluate trajectories with ToolEval.
action_grammar: Tool: a RapidAPI-hosted service containing one or more APIs.
API document: endpoint name, description, HTTP method, required and optional parameters, request body, code snippets, and example response.
Instruction: a generated user request involving one or more APIs.
Action: a thought, API name, and parameters for one API call.
Observation: the real API response returned after an action.
Finish with final answer: the terminating action for a successful trajectory.
Finish by giving up: the terminating action for an abandoned branch.
Retriever result: a set of relevant APIs passed to ToolLLaMA for multi-round decision making.
steps: Crawl RapidAPI tools and filter unreliable or low-quality APIs.
Sample APIs and use ChatGPT to generate diverse single-tool and multi-tool instructions.
Use ChatGPT with DFSDT to search for successful multi-step solution paths with real API calls and responses.
Train a neural API retriever from generated instruction/API relevance pairs.
Finetune LLaMA-2 7B on the retained instruction/solution-path pairs to produce ToolLLaMA.
At inference, retrieve relevant APIs, let ToolLLaMA call APIs over multiple rounds, and score the resulting trajectory with ToolEval.
method.pseudocode:
api_docs = crawl_and_filter_rapidapi()
instructions = chatgpt_generate_instructions(api_docs)
paths = []
for instruction in instructions:
    path = dfsdt_search(chatgpt, instruction, relevant_apis(instruction))
    if path.passed:
        paths.append(path)
retriever = train_dense_retriever(instructions, relevant_apis)
toolllama = finetune(llama2_7b, paths)

apis = retriever(user_instruction)
trajectory = toolllama.solve(user_instruction, apis)
score = tooleval(trajectory)

claims.statement: ToolBench filters RapidAPI into 3,451 high-quality tools and 16,464 APIs across 49 categories from an initial crawl of 10,853 tools and 53,190 APIs.
caveats: The corpus depends on RapidAPI availability, quality, and temporal stability.

claims.statement: ToolBench includes large-scale generated instructions and executable solution paths, including nearly 200k qualified instruction/API relevance pairs and 126,486 instruction/solution-path pairs.
caveats: The construction relies on ChatGPT for instruction generation and trajectory annotation.

claims.statement: DFSDT improves solution-path annotation over ReAct by exploring multiple branches and allowing failed branches to be abandoned.
claims.scope: Section 2.3 and preliminary experiments in Section 3.1.
caveats: DFSDT consumes more API calls than one ReAct run; the paper compares against ReAct@N to normalize budget.

claims.statement: ToolEval defines pass rate and win rate for tool-use trajectories and reports high agreement with human annotators.
caveats: ToolEval is still an LLM-based judge, so it is not an executable ground-truth verifier.

claims.statement: The neural API retriever substantially outperforms BM25 and OpenAI Ada embeddings on ToolBench retrieval metrics.
caveats: Retrieval is evaluated on generated instruction/API pairs, not arbitrary production traffic.

claims.statement: ToolLLaMA plus DFSDT reaches near-ChatGPT tool-use performance on ToolBench and exceeds Text-Davinci-003 and Claude-2 in the paper's averages.
caveats: Most Table 4 settings use oracle APIs; only ToolLLaMA-DFSDT-Retriever uses retrieved APIs instead of ground-truth APIs.

claims.statement: ToolLLaMA generalizes to APIBench despite training on a different API and instruction domain, but oracle retrieval still matters heavily.
caveats: With the paper's own retriever, ToolLLaMA's APIBench AST accuracy is much lower than with oracle retrieval.

evidence.result: ToolBench collects 16,464 real-world RESTful APIs spanning 49 RapidAPI categories. The paper reports starting from 10,853 tools and 53,190 APIs and retaining 3,451 high-quality tools and 16,464 APIs after filtering.

The paper reports nearly 200k qualified instruction/API relevance pairs, specifically 87,413 I1, 84,815 I2, and 25,251 I3 instances, and 126,486 retained instruction/solution-path pairs after DFSDT annotation.
DFSDT pass rates are 58.0 on I1, 70.6 on I2, 62.8 on I3, and 63.8 average, compared with ReAct at 37.8, 40.6, 27.6, and 35.3 average, and ReAct@N at 49.4, 49.4, 34.6, and 44.5 average.
ToolEval uses pass rate and win rate. The paper reports 87.1% agreement with human annotators for pass rate and 80.3% agreement for win rate.
The API retriever reports average NDCG@1 78.0 and NDCG@5 84.9, compared with BM25 at 18.5 and 17.0 and Ada at 49.6 and 45.4.
Average pass/win rates: ChatGPT+DFSDT 64.8/64.3, GPT-4+DFSDT 71.1/70.4, Text-Davinci-003+DFSDT 43.1/46.3, Claude-2+DFSDT 22.6/43.5, ToolLLaMA+DFSDT 66.7/60.0, and ToolLLaMA+DFSDT-Retriever 67.3/63.1.
evidence.metric: average pass rate and win rate

evidence.result: On APIBench, ToolLLaMA with its own retriever reports AST accuracy 16.77 on HuggingFace, 51.16 on TorchHub, and 40.59 on TensorHub. With oracle retrieval it reports 88.80, 85.88, and 88.62, while Gorilla-RS+Oracle reports 89.27, 93.01, and 94.16.

agent_infra_takeaways: The tool registry is data infrastructure: every endpoint needs method, parameters, request body, code snippets, example responses, and quality checks.
Multi-tool agents need execution traces, not just API-call labels. ToolBench stores thought, action, parameters, observation, and final-answer steps.
Search strategy matters. DFSDT is a runtime planning primitive because it supports branch abandonment and recovery from bad tool calls.
Retrieval is part of the action space. The model's reachable tools depend on retriever quality, so retriever evaluation belongs in the agent CI loop.
LLM-as-judge can scale evaluation, but executable checks and human audits remain necessary where side effects or correctness matter.
API temporality is unavoidable: ToolEval and ToolBench both acknowledge that RapidAPI versions, availability, responses, and reliability can change.
caveats: ToolBench depends heavily on ChatGPT for instruction generation, solution-path annotation, and evaluation.
ToolEval is not a formal verifier; it approximates human judgment using a prompted model.
The paper's strongest ToolBench main results mostly use oracle APIs, while production settings require retrieval.
RapidAPI endpoints can disappear, slow down, change schemas, or return low-quality responses over time.
ToolLLaMA's APIBench generalization improves dramatically with oracle retrieval, which shows retrieval remains a major bottleneck.
The paper focuses on tool-use capability, not authentication, authorization, rate limits, rollback, or safe side-effect execution.

related_work.title: ReAct
related_work.note: ToolLLM compares against ReAct and adds DFSDT to recover from bad branches in multi-step API execution.

related_work.title: Gorilla
related_work.note: Gorilla focuses on API-call correctness over model-hub APIs; ToolLLM expands to RapidAPI REST APIs, multi-tool tasks, and solution-path annotation.

related_work.title: Tree of Thoughts
related_work.note: The paper explicitly relates DFSDT to tree-style reasoning, while targeting open-ended decision spaces rather than small brute-force-search tasks.

poc.note: No PoC yet - contributions welcome. A useful local PoC would build a tiny REST API catalog, retrieve candidate endpoints, run a branch-and-backtrack planner over mocked responses, and score pass/win outcomes.
